brief: A caddy that holds two jerry cans of petrol upright in the boot of my car.

requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full-x2 and bin:1,0,2~hex-bin-full-x2: two full-hex bins, each 2 stories deep (~160 mm walls) on tall 3-storey cells at (0,0) and (1,0). No jerry-can prop exists in catalog so cans shown only by wells.
measure parts 364 x 249 x 467 mm; 4-cell base plus two 3-storey towers, check_build meshClash clear, capOpenFaces + lockJoints applied.
requirements.requirement: Fits / sits stable in car boot

requirements.evidence: Parts are 3D printed in user-chosen material; configurator checks fit/collisions only and knows nothing about fuel/chemical compatibility, strength under liquid load, heat or ventilation.

finish.summary: Caddy with two deep 2-storey wells for upright cans; verified clear but no jerry-can props exist and petrol/material safety cannot be verified.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
